stances.claim: Duterte's choice of Peralta as CJ -- the most senior of the three nominees -- is consistent with the stated goal of 'instill[ing] stability' and assures a smooth transition because Peralta is an ideological partner of outgoing CJ Bersamin (voting together most but not all of the time).

Carpio's argument that the Bongbong-Leni protest should be dismissed outright (no 'substantial recovery' in Caguioa's report) is doctrinally clear, but CJ Panganiban argues 'without passing judgment on the merits' that due process must first be observed before the PET could act with finality.

Alongside celebrating the WPS arbitral award, the Philippines should explore alternative ways to uphold sovereign rights -- particularly invoking China's never-denied April 13, 2009 Note Verbale and the November 2018 MoA (60-40 sharing) -- as win-win solutions allowing resource harvest 'without loss of face for China' and 'consistent with our Constitution.'

CJ's own party-list ponencias -- Veterans Party v. Comelec (Oct 6, 2000) and Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec (June 26, 2001), limiting the system to the marginalized and underrepresented and treating the 20% allocation as directory -- were reversed by Carpio after CJ's retirement in Atong Paglaum (April 2, 2013) and Banat (April 21, 2009), 'opening the party-list floodgates.'

Despite these doctrinal differences, the Carpios and Panganibans 'remain the best of personal friends, enjoying our 95-percent harmony and overlooking our 5-percent cacophony' -- 'friends can differ without being difficult.'

notable_anecdotes: The Carpio testimonial dinner exchange: CJ describing a 'long (since 1992) and close, even if at times testy, friendship'; Carpio responding that 'we have agreed to disagree' on specific decisions adverse to a company where CJ is an independent director -- used as the column's setup for documenting the three disagreements.
Reader feedback aside: 'You're such good friends, have you really taken opposite sides?' -- modeling the column-as-public-correspondence register.

Closing aphorism: '95-percent harmony and overlooking our 5-percent cacophony... friends can differ without being difficult' -- the column's signature ending and the human counterweight to the doctrinal disagreements catalogued.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban congratulates newly appointed CJ Diosdado M. Peralta -- chosen by Duterte to 'instill stability,' and ideologically aligned with outgoing CJ Lucas P. Bersamin -- and then turns to his other reason for writing: documenting his 'long (since 1992) and close, even if at times testy, friendship' with Senior Justice Antonio T. Carpio. At Carpio's testimonial dinner, Carpio said the two were 'of one mind on important national issues' but had 'agreed to disagree' on a few specific occasions. CJ catalogues three disagreements. First, on the Bongbong-Leni election protest, Carpio dissented from the PET resolution requiring both parties to comment, arguing the protest should be dismissed outright since Caguioa's pilot-province report showed no 'substantial recovery'; CJ countered in GMA News and ANC interviews that 'without passing judgment on the merits,' due process must first be observed. Second, on the West Philippine Sea, while celebrating the arbitral award, CJ argues for alternative paths -- invoking China's never-denied April 13, 2009 Note Verbale (implied admission of PH maritime entitlements) and the November 2018 MoA for 60-40 sharing -- as win-win solutions allowing resource harvest 'without loss of face for China' and 'consistent with our Constitution.' Third, on the party-list system, Carpio reversed CJ's own ponencias (Veterans Party v. Comelec, Oct 6, 2000; Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec, June 26, 2001) in Atong Paglaum (April 2, 2013) and Banat (April 21, 2009), 'opening the party-list floodgates' by removing the marginalized-and-underrepresented requirement and making the 20% allocation mandatory. Despite these differences, the Carpios and Panganibans 'remain the best of personal friends, enjoying our 95-percent harmony and overlooking our 5-percent cacophony. Indeed, friends can differ without being difficult.'
